stem: For how long should splints be worn after a burn to help prevent contractures?

options.text: Only at night for the first 2 weeks
Continuously day and night for 3 months, then gradually withdrawn over 12 months
For 1 hour daily during physiotherapy sessions
Until the initial skin graft has taken, usually 7 to 10 days
Only during the day for the first month

explanation: Continuous splinting is required for the active scar-contraction phase after a burn, then it is reduced gradually over a prolonged period.
rationale: Hypertrophic scars continue to remodel and contract for a long time after the initial injury, so early short-term splinting is not enough.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because nighttime-only splinting for 2 weeks is too little support during the period of greatest contracture risk.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because continuous day-and-night splinting for the first 3 months helps control scar contraction, with gradual weaning over the following 12 months.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because brief splinting during physiotherapy does not provide ongoing stretch against scar tightening.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the risk of contracture persists well beyond graft take and early wound healing.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because daytime-only splinting for 1 month is not enough to control the ongoing contractile forces of a burn scar.

source.hint: Hypertrophic scars continue to model and contract for a long time.
